text:
claire: opened PR to standardize retention wording across export docs and add CLI parity examples (curl, cli, python). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1120

aj: link?

claire: PR changes: replace mixed terms with 'retention period' (customer-facing), add 'retention window' internal note for infra docs, add CLI example that mirrors python/curl output, and scrub example secrets.

priya: I'll do the Python and the CLI snippet. We should show how to pass ISO durations (P30D) and a shorthand (90).

legal: Prefer 'retention period' in public docs. If you must mention 'window' keep it in parentheses and add parenthetical about backups: "(backup copies may persist per backup policy)". Also avoid 'immediately destroyed' phrasing.

claire: Thanks. I'll keep 'retention window' only in the infra note and ensure public pages use 'retention period' and the backup parenthetical. Priya, include sample that uses `<API_KEY>` placeholder.

priya: Pushed python + cli examples to PR. python snippet: ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<API_KEY>")
for rec in client.audit.export(format="jsonl", retention="P30D"):
    print(rec)
```

priya: CLI parity example added: ```bash
redwood audit export --format jsonl --retention P30D --output export.jsonl
# or using curl
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/export \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"format":"jsonl","retention":"P30D"}' > export.jsonl
```

aj: Nice. CI link checker flagged a redirect for `/docs/cli` -> should be `/sdk/cli/quickstart`. Also found old `/privacy/export` link.

linkchecker-bot: Broken/redirected links found in PR #1120: `/docs/cli` -> `/sdk/cli/quickstart`, `/privacy/export` -> `/policies/export`. Refer to CI: https://ci.redwood/links/1120

claire: I'll update the links and tweak legal phrasing: change 'data destroyed' -> 'deleted from active storage' and append backup parenthetical.

legal: Small request: add a brief instruction for support to pseudonymize actor identifiers in exported files by default (hash or truncate), and point to the pseudo-id utility in infra docs.

priya: Added a short pseudonymize snippet in the migration note: `actor_id = hash(actor_email)` example. Also replaced literal tokens with `<API_KEY>` placeholders across the PR.

docs-bot: docs-bot: CI checks running for PR #1120

linkchecker-bot: PR #1120 link check: PASS

claire: Merged. I'll follow up with a changelog bullet and an internal support playbook note about the CLI equivalence and pseudonymization guidance.
